raw_case_text:
A 26-year-old man was referred to the emergency outpatient department for low blood pressure. He has been presenting high-grade fever (39,4  C) over the last four days associated with chills, myalgias, calf pain, joint pain, and dull aching abdominal pain. He had a history of shortness of breath for one day and rashes on the lower limbs. There was no history of cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, or any bleeding manifestations. There were no associated comorbidities.
On examination, he was conscious and well-oriented to time, place, and person. His pulse rate was 130/min and regular, respiratory rate 45/min, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg on noradrenaline, and SpO2 was 82% on 50% FiO2. A non-blanchable petechial rash was observed over bilateral hands and feet. An eschar was seen in the right groin region. The liver was enlarged and palpable up to 3 cm below the right costal margin with a smooth outline on abdominal examination. There was no splenomegaly or free fluid. An abdomen ultrasound showed normal-echotexture hepatomegaly with a span of 17.5 cm (RR;<16 cm). Both kidneys showed raised cortical echogenicity. Sinus tachycardia was observed in the electrocardiogram. Serology workup for dengue, leptospirosis, hepatitis B, and C was negative. The smear for malarial parasite was negative.
The laboratory findings on admission showed a hemoglobin 13.7 gm/dL (reference range [RR]; 13.8-17.2 gm/dL); total leukocyte count of 19,500 cell/mm3 (RR; 4,500-11,000 cells/mm3); platelet count of 21x103 cells/mm3 (RR;150-450x103 cells/mm3); serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (RR;0.8-1.2 mg/dL); urea 100 mg/dl (RR; 6-24 mg/dl); AST/ALT-172/189U/L (RR; 7-55/8-48 U/L); PT/APTT-18/ 50 seconds (RR;10-12/30-40 seconds); INR-1.33 (RR;<1.1); CKMB-201 ng/ml (RR-26-192 ng/ml). The urinalysis was normal.
The possibility of tropical illness was considered and treated with intravenous ceftriaxone, doxycycline, and vasopressors. Because of persistent shock and respiratory distress, he was shifted to the respiratory intensive care unit and intubated. A second inotrope was added. Despite all supportive measures, his vitals declined, and he went into asystole. The resuscitation was unsuccessful and could not be revived. The patient was hospitalized for one and a half day.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old man presented with hypotension following a 4-day history of high-grade fever (39.4 C) with chills, myalgias, calf pain, arthralgia, and dull abdominal pain, and a 1-day history of dyspnea and lower-limb rash.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Previously healthy man developed 4 days of high-grade fever (39.4 C), chills, generalized and calf myalgias, arthralgias, and dull abdominal pain, followed 1 day prior to referral by acute shortness of breath, lower-limb petechial rash, and hypotensive shock.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high-grade fever (39.4 C), chills, myalgias, calf pain, joint pain, dull abdominal pain, shortness of breath, and hand/foot petechial rash. Negative for cough, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, or overt bleeding.

objective.physical_examination: Conscious and oriented; regular pulse 130/min, respiratory rate 45/min, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg on noradrenaline, SpO2 82% on 50% FiO2, non-blanchable petechial rash over bilateral hands and feet, a pathognomonic eschar in the right groin, and smooth hepatomegaly palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin without splenomegaly or ascites.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 13.7 g/dL (RR 13.8-17.2), leukocytosis with TLC 19,500 cells/mm3 (RR 4,500-11,000), severe thrombocytopenia with platelets 21 x 10^3 cells/mm3 (RR 150-450 x 10^3), serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (RR 0.8-1.2), urea 100 mg/dL (RR 6-24), AST 172 U/L (RR 7-55), ALT 189 U/L (RR 8-48), PT 18 s (RR 10-12), aPTT 50 s (RR 30-40), INR 1.33 (RR <1.1), CK-MB 201 ng/mL (RR 26-192), and normal urinalysis. ECG showed sinus tachycardia; abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly (17.5 cm span) and bilaterally increased renal cortical echogenicity. Malaria peripheral smear and serologies for leptospirosis, hepatitis B, and hepatitis C were negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Fulminant scrub typhus complicated by septic shock, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), severe thrombocytopenia, coagulopathy, and multiorgan dysfunction, clinically confirmed by the pathognomonic right inguinal eschar after ruling out dengue, leptospirosis, malaria, and viral hepatitis by negative serologies/smear. Treated in the respiratory ICU with mechanical ventilation, IV ceftriaxone, IV doxycycline, and dual vasopressors, but he suffered refractory shock and fatal asystole 36 hours after admission.
